Invoke plan-critic with `itération <ITERATION+1>/<PLAFOND>`. At the `reopen` or the replanning of a task already judged, the executor writes `specs.py add --task T-NNN --kind decision "plafond critique : nouveau cycle"` before the first plan-critic.
**Rule (2), exception R3** (S-01M4ZG7Q5FAHQFVKG10Y81ZYXH, S-01M51M3X9SFEZECT1QJ0XJ8GD6): in the kit, at `VOIE_COURTE=oui` the planner writes the correcting line of every blocking finding, ONE `passage court` of plan-critic judges only whether each line closes its finding, and on its GO or GO_AVEC_RESERVES the executor approves without the human gate — the lines become mandatory fixes and its reserves non-blocking items of the dev's mandate, checked at closing, security-code-review stays mandatory on the diff — which overrides rules 1 and 2; a line it leaves open goes back to the planner alone, unless a blocking finding falls in the R3 line's five blocking classes (kickoff SKILL), which send the plan back to the full loop; outside the kit never: the pilot decides at the plafond.

`security-code-review` is class-1: its HIGH/CRITICAL findings go back to `dev-*` — mandatory, never waivable. Under today's regime it is SYSTEMATIC after every dev stage that produced code (skip only docs-only tasks), `security-orchestrator` whenever a dependency manifest moved.

**`LECON_CANDIDATE` capture.** When `exec-critic` returns a `LECON_CANDIDATE` other than `aucune`, it is recorded with `python .agents/bin/retro.py add` — **as soon as that script exists (P3, T-00000330)**. Until then, the lesson stays in the verdict that wrote it: never hand-write `retro/LESSONS.md`.

For a repo-wide sweep, never one mega-plan: emit a SHARDED PLAN — one scoped sub-task per module (enumerated from `CODEBASE_INDEX.md` / the `SYMBOLS_<module>.md` shards that `build_index.py` produces), run in waves of at most the `PEUT_AJOUTER` of `charge_poste.py verdict` (a shard that neither touches another shard's files nor consumes its output joins the same wave), plus a final RECONCILE sub-task for cross-module seams. Each shard runs the SAME gated chain as any other task (`planner` → `plan-critic` → `[GATE humain unique]` → `dev-*` → `exec-critic` ∥ security → `build_index --if-stale` → `documenter`), scoped to its module only: **sharding narrows the SCOPE, never the chain**, and no shard skips `plan-critic` or `exec-critic`. The per-shard chain ENDS at `documenter` (and `indexer`); the closing review, its fixes, the gate and `tasks.py done` run ONCE per wave, serially, on the union of the wave's diffs — never one gate per shard in parallel (a critic's trace credits every `running` member of the group). Every `done` of the wave follows ONE frozen green; the push gate on the post-`done` state commit comes AFTER the last `done`, or every borrowed proof expires. RECONCILE is the terminal wave: its own review → fixes → gate → `done`.

End the routing plan with a `FORECAST` block — one `<agent> <one-line job> ~Nk` row per pipeline agent from `.agents/ref/TOKEN_BUDGETS.md`, then `TOTAL (rough) ~Nk ±50%` (use `~?` if the budgets file is missing).
